A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TRACE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original material can be matched across versions, including relocated figures and retained experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original TRACE evaluations, architecture and training-data ablations, and fine-tuning results for video captioning, moment retrieval, and highlight detection in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original general-video and event-reasoning evaluations, TRACE-uni results, and slot-count experiments in Appendices B and C.

M1.justification: The event representation, separate timestamp/score encoders and heads, interleaved decoding, head-switching mechanism, and backbone architecture remain unchanged. TRACE-uni uses additional training data; the slot-count variation is an ablation. Causality-graph integration is proposed as future work.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluations on MVBench, VideoMME, E.T.Bench, and Event-Bench, extending coverage to broader video understanding and temporal, causal, contextual, and episodic reasoning. TRACE-uni also incorporates general-video training data from the PerceptionTest and YouTube portions of LLaVA-Video-178k. Original dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The original comparison sets remain intact. New comparisons include VideoLLaMA2 on general-video benchmarks; VideoLLaMA2, Qwen2-VL, and GPT-4o on E.T.Bench; and Video-LLaVA, VideoChat2, ST-LLM, VIM, Gemini-1.5-Pro, and GPT-4o on Event-Bench. These are reported comparator rows, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: Existing experiments retain their stated splits, metrics, training budgets, and fine-tuning schedule. The new slot-count experiment compares 8 versus 16 slots while fixing 64 frames and VTG-IT-only stage-2 training. E.T.Bench adds task-specific Acc/F1/Sim/Rec reporting, although detailed protocols for the new benchmarks are sparse.

E4.justification: Tables 7–8 extend the training-data ablation with TRACE-uni, testing whether additional general-video data benefits grounding. Tables 13–14 add slot-count sensitivity analysis. The original architecture, frame-count, and training-data analyses, together with the Figure 11 case study, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. v3 maintains this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original results in Tables 2–5 and 9, and the original rows of Tables 7–8, are unchanged. v3 adds extensive benchmark, TRACE-uni, and slot-count results. For example, Table 10 newly reports MVBench/VideoMME scores of 48.1/43.8 for TRACE and 53.8/49.6 for TRACE-uni. The latter uses expanded training data, so these are additional configuration results rather than revised same-setting measurements.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises Eq. 1's defined object from the video itself to the instruction-conditioned model response. Eq. 2's factorization remains unchanged. Appendix C mostly restates the mathematics, but its new Eq. 4 conditions on e1:i, including the event being predicted, inconsistently with Eq. 2's preceding-event conditioning. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the framework's description from representing videos as events to representing video-LLM outputs as events. The central TRACE contribution and headline zero-shot and fine-tuned performance claims, including their numerical margins, remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix C distinguishes autoregressive event generation from complete causal-relationship discovery and explains inter-event and intra-event dependencies. The conclusion now explicitly acknowledges decoder-only limitations and discusses causality graphs, generated reasoning intermediates, and attention changes as future extensions. Appendix B also adds interpretations concerning general-data transfer and the slot-capacity versus computation tradeoff.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 identifies TRACE-uni's PerceptionTest/YouTube training-data selection and an approximate 2M training-data scale, and documents controls for the slot experiment. The original hardware, hyperparameters, training durations, annotation formats, processing instructions, and model/code access statement are retained.

R1.justification: Beyond retaining the original VTG and video-LLM literature, v3 substantially expands positioning against causal modeling and discovery research in Appendix C. It discusses VAR, learnable Markov logic networks, MECD, and causal-reasoning benchmarks, alongside new video-LLM, training-data, and benchmark citations.

P1.justification: The main section order and most original prose remain intact. v3 makes targeted changes to the abstract, introduction, formulation, and conclusion; expands Appendix B; and appends a structured discussion in Appendix C. Author information, acknowledgments, and appendix navigation also change.

P2.justification: The ICLR format changes typography, margins, and placement throughout. Figures 1–11 are retained but resized or relocated; Tables 7–8 gain rows, and Tables 10–15 add displays, including Table 12's expanded repetition of Table 2. Table 2's model-name caption is corrected, while Table 14 introduces an inconsistent dataset label.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the paper with quantitative general-video and event-reasoning evidence beyond v1's grounding-focused evaluation and single general-caption case. The additional ablations and explicit distinction from causal discovery also improve validation and scope clarity. These benefits outweigh the new equation and caption inconsistencies, but sparse protocols for the added evaluations and some prose comparisons lacking corresponding table entries limit the strength of the broader conclusions.
